findings.practical_consequence: A fresh planner cannot write the complete replacement without rereading and reinterpreting all 25 directives because the package supplies only short disposition summaries, not the required per-directive rationale, protected intent, activation condition, authorized action, prohibition, and stop condition; it also gives G11 two different dispositions.
evidence: requirements.json CUR-001 acceptance requires every current directive to be decomposed into protected intent, mandatory actions, prohibited actions, activation condition, and stop condition.
requirements.json FUT-005 acceptance requires every G0-G24 mapping row to contain rationale, preserved intent, activation condition, authorized action, prohibition, and stop condition.

candidate-round-1.json research_markdown `Complete G0-G24 disposition` has only Current, Disposition, and Preserved general contract columns; the absent fields are deferred to the statement that each replacement must preserve them.
candidate-round-1.json requirement_statuses FUT-005 records G11 as `move_and_retain_kernel`, while the research_markdown table records G11 as `Split`.

findings.practical_consequence: A planner cannot encode deterministic conflict handling because the package does not give one stable ordering for system, developer, repository, and user authority; implementing either version could make repository-local text improperly outrank an explicit user authorization or omit the developer boundary.
evidence: requirements.json FUT-001 acceptance requires one deterministic winner for every conflict class.
candidate-round-1.json requirement_statuses FUT-001 starts with `platform/system safety and repository instructions` and contains no developer authority level.

candidate-round-1.json research_markdown instead starts with `Platform/system safety, permissions, and developer/repository instructions`, adding developer authority while still collapsing repository instructions into the same level.

AGENTS.md states that higher-priority Codex system or developer instructions override the repository directives; it does not establish repository instructions as identical in authority to platform/system instructions. The candidate supplies no separate conflict matrix resolving repository instructions against explicit user authorization.
